violations.title: Food Manager Certificate & Responsibility
violations.observation: There is no Certified Food Manager present at the beginning of the inspection.
violations.corrective_action: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager. It is highly suggested that you have more than one employee with the food manager's license. ORS Interactive, Inc. (see handout provided) issues the required photo identification card with proof of successful completion of a certified food manager's exam. Failure to have a certified food manager on site during ALL hours of operation including food preparation, food service, and cleaning/sanitizing of equipment/utensils will result in closure of the establishment. CDI: CFM showed up during inspection. EHS instructed CFM to always have a CFM present during operation. EHS instructed CFM to prioritize getting the CFM certification for another employee. EHS will follow up for compliance,

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.'
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. CDI: EHS emailed CFM copy of the employee health policy to review information with food employees, sign the document, and maintain on file for future reference.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. CDI: EHS will email CFM copy of the written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at the handwashing sink across front the cook line in the upstairs kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. CDI: CFM placed paper towels at the hand sink across from the cook line in the upstairs kitchen.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: raw shelled eggs stored above uncooked ground beef inside the Tafco walk in refrigerator upstairs kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). CDI: CFM relocated raw shelled eggs to bottom shelf inside the Tafco walk in refrigerator.

violations.title: Food Contact Surfaces Clean to Sight & Touch
violations.observation: The following equipment/utensils were observed soiled to sight and touch: Hobart meat grinder (interior and exterior attachments) components in the upstairs kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to the sight and touch. A surface that is soiled cannot be effectively sanitized. EHS instructed CFM to clean the interior and exterior components of the Hobart meat grinder in the upstairs kitchen area.

violations.title: Non-TCS Food Contact Surface, Clean per Manufacturer
violations.observation: Observed pink mold like debris on the interior of the ice machine and not being cleaned as required in the downstairs kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is NOT time/temperature control for safety food such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, beverage and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending equipment at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. EHS instructed CFM to frequently clean ice machine to prevent accumulation of debris.

violations.title: RTE TCS Commercially Processed Food, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is commercially processed is not used or discarded within 24 hours of when the original container was opened and is not observed to be date marked: open package of shredded mozzarella cheese inside the Talfco walk in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety commercially processed foods when opened and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of the original container was opened. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. This date cannot exceed any manufacturer determined 'use-by' date based on food safety. CDI: CFM place a date marked label on open pack of shredded mozzarella cheese with remaining hold date before discard (5 remaining days).

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: prepared ground beef dish and sautéed vegetables and tomato dish stored inside the Talfco walk in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. CDI: EHS instructed CFM to place date marked label with remaining hold date before discard (6 remaining days).

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Storage of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials (chemical spray bottle) is stored above clean, in-use glasses on shelf in the bar area.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored below food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items to prevent contamination. CDI: CFM relocated chemical spray bottle to location away from clean food contact surfaces.

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: Observed frozen salmon improperly thawing in uncut ROP packaging inside the Tafco walk in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: EHS instructed CFM to cut salmon/ fish from ROP packaging to allow for proper thawing.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: multiple squeeze bottles (olive oil and pomegranate sauce), plastic containers storing dry food items (cocoa powder, almonds, flour, sugar, salt, dry powder seasoning, etc) on the upstairs cook and prep line,
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS instructed CFM to label food items removed from original container with common food name.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Controlling Pests, Eliminate Harborage Conditions
violations.observation: Harborage conditions exist. Piles of trash stored in parking lot on the side of the building attracting excessive flies in the area.
violations.corrective_action: Insects and other pests are capable of transmitting disease to people by contaminating food and food-contact surfaces. Eliminate harborage conditions to control and prevent the presence of pests on the premises. EHS will follow up on trash removal.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Bulk food containers stored on the floor inside the Talfco walk in refrigerator and box of onions stored on the food under prep counter in the upstairs kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. CDI: CFM relocated bulk food containers to shelf inside the walk in refrigerator and the box of onions to dry storage shelf in the kitchen.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Clean Utensils Storage and Handling
violations.observation: Two pallets of clean utensils (metal spoons and forks) were found stored with the food or lip-contact surface going in different directions.
violations.corrective_action: Single-service items and cleaned/sanitized utensils shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of food and lip contact surfaces are prevented. EHS instructed CFM to arrange metal utensils with handles all facing the same direction when storing.

violations.title: Equip/Utensils Self-Draining Position/Covered/Inverted
violations.observation: Observed ice bin that have been cleaned not stored covered or inverted on the floor in the downstairs kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: Clean equipment and utensils shall be stored covered or inverted to prevent contamination. CDI: CFM relocated ice bin to clean food contact surfaces inverted.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items, Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Plastic clam-shell to-go boxes were found stored not covered or inverted on shelf at the appetizer prep area upstairs kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Cleaned equipment and utensils, laundered linens, and single-service items shall be stored in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches off the floor on NSF approved shelving units or dunnage racks. EHS instructed CFM to cover or invert plastic clam-shell to- go boxes on clean contact surface.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not corrosion resistant, nonabsorbent, and/or smooth: sticker on the Revor hookah burner (upstairs hookah room) and sticker on top exterior of the ice machine downstairs kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. EHS instructed CFM to remove sticker from the revor hookah burner (upstairs hookah room) and sticker on top exterior of the ice machine downstairs kitchen area to allow equipment to be easily cleanable,

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction

EHS instructed CFM to seal/ paint exposed wood in the upstairs kitchen near the 3 vat sink to allow to be easily cleanable.

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Smooth, Easily Cleanable
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not finished to have a smooth, cleanable surface: rusted cast iron mini skillets stored on shelves above M3 3 Dr prep top refrigerator ion the prep line in the upstairs kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be finished to have a smooth, easily cleanable surface. EHS instructed CFM to discontinue using rusted mini cast iron skillets.

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Corrosion-Resistant/Nonabsorbent Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not durable: paper towel lining metal container of food inside the Tafco walk-in refrigerator and metal pan of cut lettuce leaves stored inside the M3 3 Dr prep to refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be durable, corrosion-resistant, and nonabsorbent. EHS instructed CFM to discontinue using paper towels to line food containers.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not corrosion resistant, nonabsorbent, and/or smooth: cardboard lining dry goods shelf across from fryers upstairs kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. EHS instructed CFM to remove cardboard lining dry goods shelf across from fryers upstairs kitchen to allow to be easily cleaned.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: shelves inside the Talfco walk in refrigerator upstairs main kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. EHS instructed CFM to clean shelves inside the Talfco walk in refrigerator in the upstairs main kitchen.

out_items.name: Garbage and refuse properly disposed, facilities maintained

violations.title: Refuse/Recyclables/Returnables, Removal Frequency
violations.observation: Refuse containers (multiple garbage trash bags) are stored full overnight in the parking lot on the side of the building causing an attractant to pests (excessive flies) in between trash pickup.
violations.corrective_action: Refuse, recyclables, and returnables shall be removed from the premises at a frequency that will minimize the development of objectionable odors and other conditions that attract and harbor insects and rodents. EHS instructed CFM to increase trash pick up frequency so trash bags are not improperly stored in the parking lot and attracting flies.
